Cautious but stabilizing. The statement highlights significant downside risks from COVID-19, consistent with evidence that pandemics raise economic policy uncertainty and depress investment and hiring, while weak demand and lower oil prices restrain inflation in sticky-price settings. At the same time, the Fed’s explicit shift to average inflation targeting (Powell, Jackson Hole 2020) is a “makeup” strategy that aims to re-anchor expectations at 2% after persistent undershoots (Clarida’s Taylor-principle framework), and its continued use of zero lower bound tools—forward guidance, QE in Treasuries and agency MBS, repo and ON RRP facilities—aligns with research showing these instruments ease financial conditions by lowering term premia and shaping expectations, with spillovers through integrated world financial markets. Given the mix of risk-aware language (negative) and strong, credible accommodation (mitigating), the overall tone is slightly negative but less so than a headline read of the risks alone.
